_about: AI-assisted: researched and assembled with ChatGPT (OpenAI). See docs/AI_USAGE.md. Historical snapshots from 2005–2017 U.S. DEA, Treasury, OFAC and State Department records. Charges and sanctions are distinct from convictions; financial affiliates are not labeled UWSA commanders. Myanmar is mapped only for the eight DEA-named leaders with country-level historical operating evidence. No live positions, routes, private locations, or unlicensed photos.

sources.title: Eight High-Ranking Leaders of Southeast Asia’s Largest Narcotics Trafficking Organization Indicted
sources.claim: DEA identifies the United Wa State Army as the organization of eight individually named leaders it charged in a 2005 heroin and methamphetamine trafficking indictment; the alleged conduct centered historically in eastern Burma.

people.name: Wei Hsueh Kang
people.roleLabel: Special adviser to UWSA Central Committee; formerly a division commander; 2005 U.S. narcotics indictee; OFAC listing checked September 2026

evidence.claim: The DEA identifies Wei Hsueh Kang among the indicted UWSA leaders who made decisions about the organization’s narcotics activities in eastern Burma; this is a historical country association, not a live position.
